newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia stocks advance, Philippine shares soar.
newsitem.headline: Asia stocks advance, Philippine shares soar.

text.p: Most Asian stock markets advanced on Monday, propelled by gains on Wall Street where the latest economic news and an agreement to balance the budget heartened investors.

Stocks rallied in the Philippines, where share prices had taken a beating in recent weeks amid fears of a real estate melt-down and weak corporate earnings. However, analysts questioned the strength of the recovery.
Tokyo's markets were closed for a holiday, but Hong Kong was open and traders sent the Hang Seng Index ahead in a follow through to New York's gains.
By midday, the Index was up 2.15 percent, or 280.62 points at 13,362.32.
"The market should go higher due to the better tone to U.S. stocks," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 94.72 points to close at 7,071.20 on Friday after news of an accord on the balanced budget agreement bolstered sentiment.

Although new economic data revealed signs of a tight labour market -- the unemployment rate dropped to 4.9 percent -- traders were heartened by a smaller-than-expected rise of 142,000 in non-farm payrolls.
The data, however, did not quash the debate among economists over whether the Federal Reserve will push interest rates up when policy makers meet again on May 20.
A Reuters poll in New York showed 22 of 29 economists expected the Fed to hike rates another quarter of a percentage point at the meeting.
In the Philippines, a burst of bargain-hunting fuelled a rise of more than five percent in the main stock index, but dealers stopped short of saying the worst was over.
The index closed up 130.77 points, or 5.02 percent, at the day's high of 2,736.42.
"We have to wait and see before we can say that this is not just a technical rebound. A one-day rise does not signify a reversal," said Spencer Yap, analyst at BPI Securities Corp.

The buying spree lifted shares of Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc and its housing arm Empire East Land Hondings Inc, which had suffered badly in recent weeks after fears of an oversupply in the property sector surfaced.
Indonesian shares were up a modest 2.142 points, or 0.33 percent, at 650.036 in quiet trading.
A report, released on Sunday in Canada, found the Busang gold discovery in Indonesia, touted as one of the biggest gold finds, had been based on falsified data.
But traders said there were no publically traded Indonesian firms involved in the project.
Brokers in Australia predicted a mild negative effect on the Australian gold sector following the Busang reports.
Australian stocks lost their early enthusiasm to gain only 2.7 points, or 0.12 percent, to close at 2,494.5.
Taiwan shares were hurt by fears over rising crime and political instability. The weighted index was down 47.45 points, or 0.57 percent, at 8,267.22
Singapore shares tacked on a modest gain, with the Straits Times Index up 11.65 points, or 0.58 percent, at 2,027.88, while Malaysian shares were off 4.27 points, or 0.39 percent, at 1,093.69.
Markets in Korea and Thailand were closed for holidays.
